trial_court: Court of Ms. Sukriti Jha, JFMC (NI Act) Digital Court - 02, West District, TIS Hazari Courts, Delhi
case_name: Rishi Pal (Senior Citizen) vs Pradeep Kumar

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Rishi Pal, Proprietor M/s Goyal Timber Plywood
parties.respondent_defendant: Pradeep Kumar, C/o Mr. Shiv Singh, Prop. M/s Shiv Singh Prop. M/s 24 Print Media

facts_of_case: The complainant supplied goods to the accused and issued three cheques for payment. The cheques were dishonoured with remarks 'Funds Insufficient'. The complainant repeatedly demanded payment but the accused did not pay heed.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the accused to prove that he did not receive the legal demand notice.
legal_principles.held: At this stage, the witness is confronted with notice u/s.251 Cr.P.C., framed against him dated 13.02.2023, which states that witness/accused had received the legal demand notice Ex.CW1/9.

legal_principles.principle: A security cheque can be presented along with other cheques for encashment.
legal_principles.held: The said cheque was given as a security cheque as my partner Mr. Narender Ved had expired during Covid-19. The said cheque was given to be encashed on some future date if the need arises and the goods have been supplied to me and payment is not made.

outcome.final_order: The trial court held that the complainant had established a prima facie case and directed the accused to make payment of Rs. 3,20,000 within two weeks.
